source.title: OPRD: On-Policy Representation Distillation
source.authors: Shen-Zhi Yang; Guang-Cheng Zhu; Bo-Wen Song; Hao-Bo Wang; Ming-Xuan Xia; Xing Zheng; Ying-Fan Ma; Zhong-Qi Chen; Wei-Qiang Wang; Jun-Bo Zhao; Gang Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representation similarity and reports that it is concentrated in a low-rank subspace: similarity is poor before projector training and falls as rank increases beyond the best range. This refines the claim toward partial, condition-dependent alignment, rather than testing convergence as models scale.
record.gate_note: The study cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and prior alignment work as motivation; those cited results are not recorded as rows. It also reports downstream benchmark accuracy for distilled students, but those outcomes do not directly measure the representation similarity named in the claim. Similarity increases produced by OPRD training are deliberately induced and are not treated as evidence of spontaneous convergence.
record.test_reason: The study learns a linear map from Qwen3-1.7B-Base hidden states to the top-r PCA directions of Qwen3-4B hidden states, and reports cosine similarity across ranks 1–2048 (§3.3.1, §4.2.3, Fig. 12). This is a direct, if narrow, test of linear interchangeability (V4) and of how measured alignment depends on rank (V6, V7), using a different method from the originals. It does not argue that any version is wrong; the authors present it as confirming the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. So T2, not the reader's T5. It covers only one model pair, with no scale sweep, no seeds, no cross-modal data and no feature analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, with emphasis to correct. The paper's main conclusion concerns distillation: OPRD closes the student–teacher gap and is cheaper than output-space OPD. On representations, the authors claim heterogeneous models share a low-rank structure (95% cosine at rank 8, falling with rank). They read this as confirming the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and treat higher-rank directions as architecture-specific noise.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures cosine similarity after PCA-based teacher projection and training a student-side linear projector, rather than testing the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis measurement. It does not sweep model scale or capability. The bridge alignment is deliberately learned.
record.method_sensitivity: Projected cosine similarity varies with bridge rank: it peaks at rank 8 and decreases at higher rank. For the same-architecture pair, cosine similarity also varies with response-position selection, with early positions more aligned than the tail.

fits_no_version.finding: An RL fine-tuned descendant (JustRL-1.5B) keeps 95.42% last-layer cosine similarity with its parent (R1-distill-1.5B) on the parent's rollouts. Similarity is at least 97% over the first tokens and 91.65% over the last 50 tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL fine-tuning only mildly perturbs a model's hidden-state geometry relative to its parent; divergence concentrates in late response positions.

record.problems: The alignment evidence is limited to reported model pairs and cosine similarity. The cross-architecture similarity is measured after training a projector, and no alternate similarity metric, scale sweep, or independent-seed comparison is reported. No uncertainty estimates are given for the representation-similarity measurements.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream benchmark accuracy, response length, and lexical-diversity results in Tables 2, 4, 5, and 6 are not rows because they do not directly measure representation similarity. Figure 6's rising similarity during OPRD training is excluded because the alignment is deliberately induced by the representation-matching objective. Figure 12 reports additional ranks without textual numerical values; those values are not extracted from the figure.

untested.parts: All of it. There is one cross-architecture pair with a reported similarity and no sweep over size or capability. The authors' claim to 'confirm' the PRH rests only on this single pair.
All of it. No vision–language or paired image–caption alignment is measured.
All of it. Same-architecture models from different initialisations are only asserted to be misaligned (§3.3); this is never measured.

Stitching, relative representations and unpaired mappings are not tested. Only one same-family pair (shared tokenizer) is tested. Held-out evaluation of the learned map is not reported. The Phi-4-mini→Qwen3 bridge (r=4) reports no similarity value.
All of it. No shared neurons, SAE features or circuits are examined.
Only the projection rank is varied. No other similarity metric (CKA, mutual k-NN), neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs are tested; all inputs are DAPO-Math rollouts.

Causes are not tested. The pair shares family, tokenizer and probably training data, and the study does not separate shared data or objectives from any other explanation. No plateau with scale is tested.

missing.what: A qualitative statement, with no number, that raw hidden states of different architectures have 'empirically zero' cosine even when dimensions match. Also an unmeasured assertion that same-architecture models from different initialisations are misaligned.

record.verdict_notes: r1 is reclassified because the pre-training value reflects an untrained projector. r8–r11 concern a parent and its own RL fine-tune, so they are not convergence evidence. V6 and V7 are challenge versions, so results showing rank dependence and partial alignment support them; the reader's limits_scope labels were wrong. Caveats: there is a single same-family pair with a shared tokenizer. Cosine may be computed on the same 2K prompts used to fit the projector. Inputs are math-only rollouts. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No size or capability sweep tests whether representations of independently trained models become more aligned as models scale or improve.
No vision-language or paired image-caption representation alignment is tested.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations or seeds is reported.
Tests learned linear projectors into a shared low-rank space and direct cosine similarity for one same-architecture pair; does not test stitching, relative representations, or unpaired-data mappings.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Shows sensitivity to bridge rank and response-position selection using cosine similarity; does not compare other similarity metrics, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.

Shows incomplete alignment outside a low-rank subspace and reports a same-architecture pair with shared origin; does not experimentally separate the effects of shared data, objectives, initialization, or a common model of reality.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between projected hidden states before and after Stage 1 bridge training; this row is the before-training control.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.note: The text describes the untrained projected representations as nearly orthogonal. This is a pre-bridge control, not a test of whether a learned mapping can align them.
rows.check: The 'before Stage 1' value uses the untrained, initialised student projector, so near-orthogonality is expected by construction. It is a method baseline, not evidence about the models' alignment, and should not count toward V4, V6 or V7.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.note: The learned projection improves alignment substantially, but the reported cosine is below the best low-rank result.
rows.check: State is judged against V4: 72.3% at rank 1 is a clearly incomplete mapping. For V6 the row helps show the rank dependence. The text does not say whether cosine was computed on held-out data or on the same 2K prompts used to fit the projector.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.value: 93.7–95.0%; the text identifies rank 8 as the peak
rows.note: The study reports this rank interval as the practical operating range; rank 8 is separately reported at 95.0%.
rows.check: 93.7–95.0% over ranks 4–16 overlaps with r4; it is a range read from text and figure. Same caveat that held-out evaluation is not stated.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.note: The paper reports the rank-8 result as the peak.
rows.check: None beyond the in-sample caveat. The pair is the same family (Qwen3) with a shared tokenizer.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.note: Similarity is lower than the rank-8 peak.
rows.check: 94.1% is near the peak, so for V4 it is observed rather than partial. Being lower than the peak is not a weaker V4 effect.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.note: Similarity continues to decline as rank increases beyond the low-rank peak.
rows.check: 87.9% at rank 256: the linear map recovers less as lower-variance directions are added. For V7 this indicates the alignment is incomplete.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B teacher / Qwen3-1.7B-Base student (paired hidden representations)
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity after training the student-side linear projector against the teacher PCA basis.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between projected student and teacher representations
rows.baseline: Before Stage 1, similarity was ≤ 7.5% at all tested ranks
rows.note: The full-rank result is substantially below the low-rank peak.
rows.check: 77.0% at full rank 2048: the full-space linear map is clearly lossy. Against V7 this is consistent with partial convergence.

rows.subject: R1-distill-1.5B student / JustRL-1.5B teacher (paired hidden representations)
rows.stage_stated: Student: R1-distill-1.5B checkpoint; teacher: obtained by applying RL to R1-Distill-1.5B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between last-layer hidden states on student-generated rollouts, restricted to the first response tokens.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between student and teacher last-layer hidden states
rows.note: The paper attributes the high similarity to the early response already being aligned in this model pair.
rows.check: JustRL-1.5B is an RL fine-tune of R1-distill-1.5B, i.e. a model and its own descendant. They are not independently trained models, not different seeds, and no map is learned. The row does not bear on any version; it is moved to fits_no_version.

rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between last-layer hidden states on student-generated rollouts, restricted to the first response tokens.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between student and teacher last-layer hidden states
rows.note: The text reports this as the peak of the first-k curve.
rows.check: Parent/fine-tuned-descendant pair; same issue as r8. It is also a peak value from the same curve as r8.

rows.subject: R1-distill-1.5B student / JustRL-1.5B teacher (paired hidden representations)

rows.note: The last-k curve is reported as at least 4 points below the first-k curve until k approaches the full response length.
rows.check: Parent/fine-tuned-descendant pair; it measures where the fine-tune diverges from its parent, not convergence.

rows.subject: R1-distill-1.5B student / JustRL-1.5B teacher (paired hidden representations)
rows.stage_stated: Student: R1-distill-1.5B checkpoint; teacher: obtained by applying RL to R1-Distill-1.5B
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between last-layer hidden states across the full response.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between student and teacher last-layer hidden states
rows.note: The text says the first-k and last-k curves coincide at this full-response value.
rows.check: Parent/fine-tuned-descendant pair; same issue as r8.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-1.7B-Base → Qwen3-4B learned linear projector, ranks 4–32
relationships.reason: A linear map aligns the student to the teacher's top principal directions at 93.7–95.0% cosine (r3, r4, r5), across different depth and width.
relationships.display_finding: The projector achieved 93.7–95.0% cosine alignment with the teacher's top principal directions despite different model depths and widths.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen3-1.7B-Base → Qwen3-4B learned linear projector, ranks 4–32
source_check.reason: r3–r5 show 93.7–95.0% cosine for learned linear alignment to selected teacher PCA coordinates. Support is confined to those coordinates; full-representation preservation and held-out map performance are not established.

relationships.condition: Same pair, rank 1 and ranks ≥256 including full rank
relationships.reason: Mapping quality falls to 87.9% at r=256 and 77.0% at full rank, and is 72.3% at r=1 (r2, r6, r7). The map is close to lossless only within a few top PCA directions.
relationships.display_finding: Mapping quality was 72.3% at rank 1, 87.9% at rank 256, and 77.0% at full rank, with near-lossless recovery confined to a few leading PCA directions.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Same pair, rank 1 and ranks ≥256 including full rank
source_check.reason: r2, r6 and r7 report 72.3%, 87.9% and 77.0% cosine at ranks 1, 256 and 2048. The mapping remains substantially aligned but clearly incomplete, qualifying interchangeability rather than showing its absence.

relationships.condition: Choice of projection rank, Qwen3 pair
relationships.reason: Measured cross-model cosine ranges from 72.3% to 95.0% depending only on rank (r2–r7). Alignment weakens under other settings but does not vanish.
relationships.display_finding: Changing projection rank alone moved cross-model cosine between 72.3% and 95.0%, weakening alignment without making it vanish.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Choice of projection rank, Qwen3 pair
source_check.reason: r2–r7 show measured cosine changing with retained rank: 72.3% at rank 1, a 95.0% peak at rank 8, and 77.0% at rank 2048. This supports dependence on representation preprocessing settings.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-4B vs Qwen3-1.7B-Base, full representation space
relationships.reason: Shared structure is concentrated in about 8 principal directions, and full-rank linear alignment is only 77.0% (r6, r7). The causes of the alignment are not tested.
relationships.display_finding: Shared structure concentrated in about 8 principal directions, and full-rank linear alignment reached only 77.0%.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen3-4B vs Qwen3-1.7B-Base, full representation space
source_check.reason: r6–r7 support the partial-alignment component: cosine falls to 87.9% at rank 256 and 77.0% at the reported full rank of 2048. Plateauing with scale and explanations based on shared training data or objectives are untested.

relation.reason: The study reports representation-alignment measurements before and after bridge training across projection ranks, beyond reporting downstream distillation performance.

tranche.reason: The frozen-backbone experiment tests shared representational structure using teacher PCA and a learned student linear map, with a rank sweep; this is a different method addressing the convergence question.

source_check.notes: Held-out bridge evaluation is not reported; projected cosine does not establish reconstruction fidelity or preservation of all information. The paper calls rank 2048 full rank, but the teacher has 2560 hidden dimensions; §4.2.3 also overgeneralizes its >90% result to all ranks ≥4 despite explicitly reporting lower high-rank values.

statements.correction: Qwen3-1.7B-Base student projector versus Qwen3-4B teacher PCA coordinates: 95.0% cosine at rank 8; 77.0% at rank 2048. Held-out map evaluation not reported. V4 label for the higher-rank condition: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The Qwen3 facts are correct, but the challenges label overstates this study: alignment is incomplete at higher rank, rather than absent or reversed.
